knowledge_point.title: Identifying a Possible Slope Field Based on the Type of Equation

question.:question/problem: Given that $f(x,y)$ varies with both $x$ and $y,$ which of the following **cannot** be the slope field for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=f(x,y)?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that we are given an equation of the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=f(x,y).
$$

The right-hand side is a function of $x$ and $y.$ This means that the slope field varies with both $x$ and $y.$

Of the given slope fields, we note the following slope field does not vary with $y$ given a fixed value of $x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/repairs/2026-10-20-early-cohort/jobs/17592186172040/review-0-policy-2-4c6625aaf57ad834/runtime/package/17592186172040/plots/3eac87e7c7ee6e1d0dc0773b9e78521c7c21f414bdaff24726416d6d96e4f347.png)

 

To see this more clearly, notice that if we draw a vertical line, the slopes do not vary.
